summary.headline: RSWM Q2 FY27 revenue rose 15% YoY to ₹1,322 crore and PAT more than tripled to ₹24.5 crore, while fabric segments stayed near breakeven on raw-material cost pressure.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached ₹1,322 crore in Q2 FY27, up 13.9% QoQ and 15% YoY, with EBITDA of ₹116 crore (8.7% margin) up 47.1% YoY. PAT rose to ₹25 crore from ₹6 crore a year earlier, though this was after a one-time ₹11.5 crore exceptional provision on electricity duty for captive solar. Management said fabric (denim and knit) profitability was squeezed by cotton and polyester price spikes that could not be passed on quickly, with the fabric PBIT reported as negative ₹6 crore in the quarter. Management guided to better Q3 and Q4 on price pass-through and the ₹92 crore knitting expansion, and said H2 should beat H1.

financial_highlights.change: +23.2% QoQ; +47.1% YoY; margin +66 bps QoQ, +191 bps YoY
from ₹17 crore in Q1 FY27 and ₹6 crore in Q2 FY26

segments.name: Fabric (Denim and Knit)
segments.commentary: Management said PBIT was negative ₹6 crore in Q2, the third straight weak quarter, as cotton up about ₹60/kg equivalent and polyester up from ₹96 to ₹146 per kg were not passed on fully. Knit utilisation improved QoQ.

segments.name: Yarn (synthetic, cotton, blended, melange)
segments.commentary: Management said most spinners passed on raw-material increases largely to customers. Cotton yarn is less than one-fifth of turnover, and trading gains on cotton stock were a small part of Q2 results.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q4 FY27 to be better for fabric, with Q1 FY28 'much brighter' than Q2, and H2 FY27 to be better than H1 FY27.
Overall EBITDA margin should be around or better than 8.7% in the coming quarter; fabric division EBITDA should target double digits.

Full impact of the ₹92 crore knitting expansion (including 250 metric tonnes of additional knitted production and printing) expected in Q4 FY27, fully visible in Q1 FY28; project on track for December completion.
Revenue mix expected to shift toward roughly two-thirds yarn and one-third fabric from the current three-fourths/one-fourth split in Q1 FY28.
Standalone ROCE to improve from the current 6-6.5% level, 'this or slightly better', without a numerical target.
Standalone debt of ₹1,480 crore with ₹95 crore due in H1 FY27; annual repayment around ₹180 crore in FY28.
LNJ GreenPET (100% subsidiary, bottle-to-bottle recycling) expected to start commercial production in Q1 FY28 with about ₹200 crore revenue expected.
capex_capacity: Knitting expansion of ₹92 crore: printing and 250 metric tonnes of additional knitted production expected in Q4 FY27; project in line with timelines and cost.

LNJ GreenPET bottle-to-bottle project: commercial production expected Q1 FY28; about ₹62 crore RSWM equity, of which ₹29 crore already invested; ₹27 crore of a ₹36 crore preferential share issue from LNJ Textiles Advisory to go into bottle-to-bottle recycling.

LNJ NDS9 Global Private Limited (RSWM 74%, NDS9 26%): premium denim and knit garment manufacturing for international clients; Phase-1 investment ₹208 crore, RSWM equity about ₹46 crore; more than 12 months to complete, likely Q4 FY28 or Q1 FY29.
Management is focused on utilisation, especially in knitting and melange, and on automation and digitalisation.
demand_pricing: Cotton prices rose about ₹16,000 per candy (about ₹60/kg on cotton yarn); polyester rose from ₹96 to ₹146 over six months; gas, dyes, chemicals and freight also rose.
Order booking runs 30-40 days in knit and denim, so price increases lag cost increases; management said sale prices rose but not in line with costs.
Denim market described as good with fairly high utilisation; knit utilisation improved QoQ.
Export order flow was disrupted by West Asia tensions; apparel export demand slowed, while India's H1 textile exports grew moderately.
Management said price increases for next season are being negotiated with brands and domestic customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the fabric division (denim and knit) earning no meaningful profit for three quarters, with negative PBIT of ₹6 crore, and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to cost push from cotton, polyester, gas and chemicals, with price pass-through lagging by 30-40 days of order booking. It said the issue is temporary, Q4 should be better, and Q1 FY28 looks brighter. It also noted that PBIT losses partly reflect interest and depreciation from new capex still ramping up.

qa_highlights.question: How much surplus cash is available and where will it be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash flow after interest will first repay current loans, then fund normal capex, and then equity in the two new projects: LNJ NDS9 and LNJ GreenPET.

qa_highlights.question: What is the equity outlay in LNJ NDS9 Phase-1 and LNJ GreenPET?
qa_highlights.answer: RSWM's share is about ₹46 crore in LNJ NDS9 (of ₹208 crore Phase-1) and about ₹62 crore in LNJ GreenPET, of which ₹29 crore is already invested.

qa_highlights.question: How much incremental depreciation and interest came from new capex this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only interest has started; depreciation has not begun because the knitting project is not yet commissioned.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q2 profit came from one-off inventory or trading gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cotton trading gains from short-term price spikes are part of operations. Cotton yarn is less than one-fifth of turnover, and the company does not do speculative stocking.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fabric contribution and EBITDA margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Fabric was about 26% of Q2 revenue. Management targets double-digit EBITDA margins in fabric and said the group margin should be around or above 8.7% in the coming quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt repayment schedule and the peak debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone debt is ₹1,480 crore, with ₹95 crore due in H1 FY27 and around ₹180 crore in FY28. Management did not give a peak debt figure.

risks_watch: Fabric margins: cost pass-through lag in denim and knit; watch whether Q3 and Q4 price increases stick and whether fabric turns positive PBIT.
Execution of the ₹92 crore knitting expansion (December completion, Q4 output) and LNJ GreenPET start in Q1 FY28.
Input-cost volatility in cotton, polyester, gas and freight, plus West Asia disruption to export orders.
Exceptional item: ₹11.5 crore electricity duty provision on captive solar; ₹7.42 crore deposited under protest; SLP pending before the Supreme Court.
Quality of earnings: H1 PAT and other equity were helped by ₹181 crore fair-value gain in OCI on HEG-related equity, not operating income.
Capital allocation: equity commitments to LNJ NDS9 and LNJ GreenPET, plus ₹180 crore FY28 debt repayment, against ₹400-450 crore run-rate EBITDA as cited by an analyst.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes, the expansion timeline and the outlook for H2, but cautious and somewhat evasive on fabric margins, where management gave no numbers beyond directional improvement. Management avoided quantifying ROCE, peak debt and the fabric PBIT gap, and answered several questions only partially.
key_quotes: So, we expect at least in 4th quarter, we will be better off.
A key focus has been on prioritizing profitability over the volume -led expansion that we discussed during the last call also.
So, we should target double digits as EBITDA in fabric division, both denim and knit.

LNJ GreenPET bottle-to-bottle recycling plant (~₹200 crore revenue expected)

growth.why: Management guides H2 FY27 better than H1 and Q3 EBITDA margin around or above 8.7%, backed by the ₹92 crore knitting expansion (250 MT, due Q4 FY27, December completion) and price pass-through being negotiated, though fabric PBIT was negative ₹6 crore and no numerical revenue growth target was given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided group EBITDA margin around or better than 8.7% in the coming quarter vs 8.7% in Q2, with fabric EBITDA targeted in double digits, though fabric PBIT was negative ₹6 crore in Q2 and price pass-through is lagging 30-40 days.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: The ₹92 crore knitting expansion adds 250 MT of knitted production and printing, on track for December completion with full impact in Q4 FY27 and fully visible in Q1 FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Knit utilisation improved QoQ and the 250 MT knitting addition comes online in Q4 FY27, but no numerical volume target was given and export orders were disrupted by West Asia tensions (exports +4.5% in H1 FY27).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is already committed to LNJ NDS9 (₹208 crore Phase-1, RSWM equity ~₹46 crore) and LNJ GreenPET (~₹62 crore equity), with management directing surplus cash to these projects, but no new capex was announced and utilisation was not quantified.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said H2 FY27 should beat H1 (H1 EBITDA ₹210 crore, margin 8.4%) and Q4 and Q1 FY28 should be better, but no numerical revenue or margin guidance was raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Fabric PBIT was negative ₹6 crore for a third straight quarter, and cotton (up about ₹16,000 per candy) and polyester (₹96 to ₹146/kg) cost pressure could persist if price pass-through lags 30-40 days.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: LNJ GreenPET bottle-to-bottle recycling starts commercial production in Q1 FY28 with about ₹200 crore revenue expected, backed by ₹29 crore of ₹62 crore RSWM equity already invested.

rows.label: Fabric margin recovery via price pass-through
rows.why: Price increases for next season are being negotiated with brands and domestic customers, and fabric EBITDA is targeted at double digits, versus negative fabric PBIT of ₹6 crore in Q2 FY27.

rows.label: Debt repayment from surplus cash
rows.why: Management said surplus cash after interest will first repay current loans, with about ₹180 crore due in FY28 against standalone debt of ₹1,480 crore.

rows.label: Standalone ROCE improvement
rows.why: Standalone ROCE is 6-6.5% and management said it will be 'this or slightly better' with no numerical target, while new capex is still ramping and depreciation has not started.

tone.note: Management was confident on the knitting expansion timeline (December completion, Q4 FY27 output) and H2 outlook, but cautious and partly evasive on fabric margins, peak debt and ROCE; analysts pressed on fabric losses, cash deployment and one-offs in Q2 profit.
